19622.subject: Biology
19622.question_text: Which of the following best describes a colony of volvox?
19622.explanation:
Living cells exist in a variety of forms, including Singly or free-living, filamentous and Colonial.

A Volvox colony is made up of thousands of small biflagellate somatic cells arranged in a peripheral layer and embedded in a transparent extracellular matrix (ECM). Volvox can reproduce asexually by forming daughter colonies that are identical to the parent colony. These daughter colonies form inside the parent colony and eventually burst out, killing the parent colony. Consequently, asexually reproduced cells held together in a mass, but independent of each other, explains a colony of Volvox.

options.text: Asexually reproduced cells held together in a mass, but independent of each other
Sexually reproduced cells held together in a mass, and dependent on each other
Single free-living acellular units irrespective of their parental origin
Several units of cells, held together by cytoplasmic strands and dependent on each other

19624.subject: Biology
19624.question_text: All the following organelles have membranes except
19624.explanation:
• Cell wall

    A non-membrane-bound organelle found in plant, fungi, and some bacteria cells. The cell wall is made of carbohydrates and proteins, and its main function is to protect the cell and provide structure and support. 

  • Cell membrane

    Present in all cells, the cell membrane is made of lipids, proteins, and carbohydrates. It's the outermost layer of the cell in animals, and encloses other organelles within. The cell membrane is flexible, metabolically active, and selectively permeable. The cell wall is a non-membrane-bound organelle, while the cell membrane is present in all cells. Therefore, Cell wall has no membrane. Option D.

19625.subject: Biology
19625.question_text: Which of these has the most complex level of organization?
19625.explanation:
The levels of organization in the human body, from basic to complex are: Cell, Tissue, Organ, System, Organism. 

  • Cells

    The most basic unit of life and the smallest unit that can reproduce. 

  • Tissues

    A group of similar cells that work together to perform a specific function. The heart's cardiac muscle is a tissue. 

  • Organs

    A structure made up of different tissues that perform specific bodily functions. The heart is an organ. 

  • Organ systems

    A higher level of organization that consists of functionally related organs. The heart is part of the circulatory system, which also includes blood vessels.As a result, the heart is part of a complex system of organization in the body.

19626.subject: Biology
19626.question_text: The unit contained in a cell structure responsible for changes in form and shape of organisms is called
19626.explanation:
Genes are responsible for the physical characteristics of organisms, including their form and shape. 

Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) is a biological molecule that contains the instructions for an organism's development, growth, reproduction, and functioning. DNA is present in almost every cell in the body.

19627.subject: Biology
19627.question_text: The plant cell mostly stores food as
19627.explanation:
Plant cells store food primarily as starch, a white, granular organic chemical. Plants produce starch in their green leaves from excess glucose created during photosynthesis. When needed, plants can break down starch into glucose units for energy.

On the other hand, animal cells store food as glycogen, a polysaccharide of glucose. The hormone insulin converts excess glucose in the blood into glycogen, which is then stored in the muscles and liver. When the body needs extra energy during exercise, glycogen is broken down into glucose.

19628.subject: Biology
19628.question_text: The presence of a large member of mitochondria in a cell indicates that
19628.explanation:
Mitochondria are organelles that produce energy through oxidative phosphorylation, regulate metabolic activity, and promote cell growth and multiplication.A large number of mitochondria in a cell indicates that the cell has a high energy demand. Some different cells have different amounts of mitochondria because they need more energy. So for example, the muscle has a lot of mitochondria, the liver does too, the kidney as well, and to a certain extent, the brain, which lives off of the energy those mitochondria produce.

A large number of mitochondria in a cell indicates that the cell is active because it has a high demand for energy

19630.subject: Biology
19630.question_text: In which of the following organisms is ammonia excreted as a waste product?
19630.explanation:
Ammonia is a waste product excreted by aquatic animals, as well as some other organisms, including Amoeba.

  • Amoeba's main waste products are ammonia and carbon dioxide. It excretes waste through diffusion, which is the movement of molecules from a higher concentration to a lower concentration.

  • Other organisms excrete nitrogenous wastes in different forms, including:

  • Birds and lizards: Excrete nitrogenous wastes as uric acid 
  • Humans: Excrete urea 
  • Reptiles and many terrestrial invertebrates: Produce uric acid

19631.subject: Biology
19631.question_text: The following are the functions of supporting tissues in plant except
19631.explanation:
Supporting tissues in plants have several functions, including:

  • Structural support: Supporting tissues provide the framework and support the structure of the plant, holding up leaves, flowers, and buds. 

  • Transportation: Supporting tissues transport water, nutrients, and assimilates throughout the plant. 

  • Protection: The strength of supporting tissues protects the plant from enemies. For example, the hard shell of many seeds prevents animals from chewing them to pieces or puncturing them. 

  • Flexibility: Supporting tissues give the plant flexibility and resilience, allowing it to bend without breaking.

19632.subject: Biology
19632.question_text: Which of the following organisms has the largest surface area-to-volume ratio?
19632.explanation:
Amoeba has the largest surface area-to-volume ratio among the organisms listed in the options. This is because amoeba is a unicellular organisms with a relatively large surface area compared to their volume.

As the size of an organism increases, its volume increases faster than its surface area. This means that the surface area to volume ratio decreases as the organism gets larger.

19633.subject: Biology
19633.question_text: Which of the following plant parts does not perform supportive function?
19633.explanation:
The supporting tissues in plants are collenchyma, sclerenchyma, and vascular tissues (xylem and phloem).

Parenchyma is one of the three main types of ground tissue in plants, along with collenchyma and sclerenchyma. Collenchyma is a living support tissue with irregular walls, while sclerenchyma is a dead support tissue with thick walls.

19634.explanation: Decay in meat is not a useful effect of microorganisms. Microorganisms can cause meat to spoil, which can lead to food waste and food borne infections. Spoilage can cause meat to change color, produce off-flavors, and develop mucus and exudates.

19635.subject: Biology
19635.question_text: Which of the following structures is not present in the vascular bundles of a dicot stem?
19635.explanation: In each of vascular bundles in the dicot stem, xylem and phloem are on the same radius with xylem situated towards the pith and phloem situated towards the pericycle and a strip of cambium separates the two. This strip of cambium that separates the phloem and xylem is called interfascicular cambium. Therefore the only structure not present in the vascular bundle of a dicot stem is intrafascicular cambium. The correct answer is option C.

19636.subject: Biology
19636.question_text: When a mammal respires anaerobically for a long time
19636.explanation:
When a mammal respires anaerobically for a long time, lactic acid builds up in the muscles, leading to fatigue and cramps. 

  • Lactic acid build-up: Anaerobic respiration produces lactic acid as a waste product when glucose is broken down. This lactic acid accumulates in the muscles. 
  • Muscle fatigue: A buildup of lactic acid causes muscle fatigue. 
  • pH drop: If too much lactic acid builds up, the pH falls, which can affect enzyme function and lead to fatigue and cramps. The correct answer is option C

19642.subject: Biology
19642.question_text: The organs constantly in touch with the liver are
19642.explanation:
The liver is the largest internal organ and is situated in the upper right-hand part of the abdominal cavity. Its visceral surface (the underside) is in direct, constant contact with several organs that leave impressions on it due to their proximity. 

  • Stomach: The left lobe of the liver features a large "gastric impression" where it rests directly against the anterior surface of the stomach.
  • Gallbladder: This pear-shaped sac is physically attached to the visceral surface of the liver in a shallow depression called the gallbladder fossa.  The liver also makes contact with the duodenum, right kidney, and the transverse colon (specifically the right colic flexure). However, the stomach and gallbladder are primary anatomical neighbors frequently cited in medical and biological contexts regarding liver impressions.
